ce8730bc0a4bbcd16934af4acf5b87cf2e229384.title: Absolute upper bound and honesty
ce8730bc0a4bbcd16934af4acf5b87cf2e229384.body:
There exists an absolute constant \(K_0>0\) such that, for every choice satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arithmetic engine.)} \(\mathsf E\) is an admissible, independently fixed deterministic rational interval-arithmetic engine.
\item \textbf{(Naming policy.)} \(\mathsf N\) is an admissible Borel naming policy selecting valid names for the public exponents and observed covariates, with public exponent names fixed independently of the sample.
\item \textbf{(Public exponents.)} The public smoothness exponents satisfy
\[
0<\beta<\frac14,\qquad \beta<\alpha\le1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\) is an integer with \(n\ge1\).
\end{itemize}
the literal upper-construction output \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\) induces a measurable interval procedure and satisfies
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\) is the class of globally honest procedures in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. For every radius \(r\in[0,1/2]\) and every observed law \(P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)\), the radius model of \cref{obj:def:radius-model},
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\left[
\left|I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\right|
\right]
\le K_0\,d_n(\alpha,\beta;r),
\]
where the expectation includes the independent uniform randomization seed \(U\), with law \(\lambda\), and \(d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\) is the diagnostic envelope in \cref{obj:def:diagnostic-envelope}. The same constant \(K_0\) applies to all admissible engines and naming policies, all stated exponents and sample sizes, and all such radii and laws.

For every sample and seed, the output is a nonempty closed interval with rational endpoints: there exist \(l,u\in\mathbb Q\) such that
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)
=[l,u],
\qquad
-\frac12\le l\le u\le\frac12.
\]
At \(n=1\), for every sample and seed,
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{1,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)
=\left[-\frac12,\frac12\right].
\]

2cadd8fe0d1b301550d118574bd8a2cc3925044e.title: Projection approximation and moments
2cadd8fe0d1b301550d118574bd8a2cc3925044e.body:
Let \(P\) be an observed law with continuous, strictly interior conditional four-cell probabilities, satisfying \cref{obj:ass:uniform-design}. Let \(k\ge1\) be an integer, and let \(\Pi_k\) denote the rank-\(k\) cosine projection used in \cref{obj:def:projection-statistic}.

For every \(0<\gamma\le1\) and every continuous function \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\),
\[
\|f-\Pi_k f\|_{L^2(\lambda)}
\le 5[f]_\gamma k^{-\gamma},
\qquad
[f]_\gamma
=
\sup_{\substack{x,z\in[0,1]\\x\ne z}}
\frac{|f(x)-f(z)|}{|x-z|^\gamma}.
\]
Here \(\lambda\) is the uniform probability law on \([0,1]\), and the norm and Hölder seminorm are interpreted in the extended nonnegative reals, allowing \([f]_\gamma=+\infty\).

For every pair of measurable record marks \(W,V\) taking values in \([0,1]\), and every integer \(n\ge2\), define their conditional means using the four-cell conditional law under \(P\):
\[
w(x)=E_P[W\mid X=x],
\qquad
v(x)=E_P[V\mid X=x].
\]
For the ordered-pair statistic \(\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)\) of \cref{obj:def:projection-statistic}, evaluated on \(n\) independent original records with law \(P\),
\[
E_P\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)
=
\langle\Pi_k w,\Pi_k v\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)},
\]
\[
\langle w,v\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)}
-
E_P\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)
=
\langle w-\Pi_k w,v-\Pi_k v\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)},
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)\}
\le
\frac4n+\frac{2k}{n(n-1)}.
\]

1d47b99c549ae2271e2bcb7a64bc896d071209c9.title: Observable odds and causal interpretation
1d47b99c549ae2271e2bcb7a64bc896d071209c9.body:
Let \(0<\beta<1/4\) and \(\beta<\alpha\leq1\), and let \(P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), the model class in \cref{obj:def:model}. Write \(\lambda\) for the uniform probability law on \([0,1]\), and define the observable coordinates
\[
C(P)
=
E_P[AY]
-
\int_{[0,1]} e(P,x)\,E_P[Y\mid X=x]\,\lambda(dx),
\qquad
S(P)
=
\int_{[0,1]}
P(A=1,Y=0\mid X=x)\,
P(A=0,Y=1\mid X=x)\,\lambda(dx),
\]
where \(e(P,x)\) is the conditional treatment probability. With
\[
\theta(P)=\operatorname{logit}\mu_1(P,0)-\nu(P,0),
\qquad s_0=\frac{1}{512},
\]
where \(\mu_1(P,0)\) is the treated-arm risk at zero and \(\nu(P,0)\) is the control-arm prognosis logit at zero, one has
\[
C(P)=\{\exp(\theta(P))-1\}S(P),
\qquad
S(P)\geq s_0,
\qquad
\theta(P)=\log\{1+C(P)/S(P)\}.
\]

For every Markov kernel \(\Gamma\) from \([0,1]\) to \(\{0,1\}^2\) whose first and second margins at every \(x\) are Bernoulli laws with means
\[
P(Y=1\mid A=0,X=x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
P(Y=1\mid A=1,X=x),
\]
respectively, the full-data law \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) of \cref{obj:def:causal-extension} has the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed law and consistency.)}
The image of \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) under
\[
((x,(y^0,y^1)),a)\longmapsto
\bigl(x,a,(1-a)y^0+ay^1\bigr)
\]
is \(P\). For every full-data record,
\[
Y=(1-A)Y^0+AY^1.
\]

\item \textbf{(Construction and conditional exchangeability.)}
The law \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) is the successive kernel composition obtained by drawing \(X\) from \(\lambda\), drawing \((Y^0,Y^1)\) from \(\Gamma(P,X)\), and drawing \(A\) from the observed-law treatment kernel with Bernoulli mean \(e(P,X)\). Under its full conditional law at every \(x\in[0,1]\), the pair \((Y^0,Y^1)\) and \(A\) are independent.

\item \textbf{(Conditional causal log-odds.)}
For every \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
\operatorname{logit}
\left(\int_{\{0,1\}^2} y^1\,\Gamma(P,x)(d(y^0,y^1))\right)
-
\operatorname{logit}
\left(\int_{\{0,1\}^2} y^0\,\Gamma(P,x)(d(y^0,y^1))\right)
=
\theta(P).
\]

\item \textbf{(Full conditional disintegration.)}
Composing \(\lambda\) with the full conditional laws of \(((Y^0,Y^1),A)\) at \(x\), then taking the image under the canonical reassociation
\[
\bigl(x,((y^0,y^1),a)\bigr)
\longmapsto
\bigl((x,(y^0,y^1)),a\bigr),
\]
gives exactly \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\).
\end{itemize}

f77055b48368c834cd9eda7c976c9ba8517332e1.title: Parametric lower bound on length
f77055b48368c834cd9eda7c976c9ba8517332e1.body:
Let \(\alpha,\beta,r\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exponent domain.)} \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), the public exponent domain given by
\[
\mathcal D=\{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R^2:0<\beta<1/4,\ \beta<\alpha\le1\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(0\le r\le1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then the minimax expected interval length \(J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\) defined in \cref{obj:def:length-objective} satisfies
\[
J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\ge \frac{3}{16}n^{-1/2}.
\]

a27ac049240433094ded5a8e1cf066fd9b77ad85.title: Scalar implicit function theorem
a27ac049240433094ded5a8e1cf066fd9b77ad85.body:
Let \(d\) be a nonnegative integer, let \(F:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), and let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R\). Fix \(\mathbf b_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\chi_0\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Open domain.)} \(D\) is open and \((\mathbf b_0,\chi_0)\in D\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(F\) is continuously differentiable on \(D\).
\item \textbf{(Zero.)} \(F(\mathbf b_0,\chi_0)=0\).
\item \textbf{(Nonzero partial derivative.)} \(\partial_\chi F(\mathbf b_0,\chi_0)\ne0\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist open sets \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(V\subseteq\mathbb R\), and a function \(q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), such that
\[
\mathbf b_0\in U,\qquad \chi_0\in V,\qquad U\times V\subseteq D.
\]
The function \(q\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\), satisfies \(q(\mathbf b_0)=\chi_0\), and has \(q(\mathbf b)\in V\) for every \(\mathbf b\in U\). Moreover, for every \(\mathbf b\in U\) and every \(\chi\in V\),
\[
F(\mathbf b,\chi)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\chi=q(\mathbf b).
\]

13c727a7cfb0bf93ea263356caca0b27441e7c3c.title: Sharp honest length frontier
13c727a7cfb0bf93ea263356caca0b27441e7c3c.body:
There exist absolute constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c\) and \(0<C\), for which the following assertions hold. Write
\[
\mathcal D=\{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R^2:0<\beta<1/4,\ \beta<\alpha\le1\},
\]
the domain of public smoothness exponents, and define the numerator and denominator exponents and the expected-length profile by
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)
=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},
\qquad
\mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1},
\qquad
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}+r n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)}.
\]

For every choice satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arithmetic engine.)} \(\mathsf E\) is an admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine.
\item \textbf{(Naming policy.)} \(\mathsf N\) is an admissible Borel policy selecting valid names for the public exponents and observed covariates.
\item \textbf{(Exponents and sample size.)} \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\) satisfies \(n\ge1\).
\end{itemize}
the attaining interval is the upper-construction output
\[
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta).
\]
This output is a deterministic, radius-independent Borel procedure belonging to the globally \(90\%\)-honest class \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\) of \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. It returns a nonempty closed connected interval in \([-1/2,1/2]\) with rational endpoints after the two prescribed finite precision budgets and finite rational arithmetic. Its inputs are the fixed engine, the public exponents and their valid names, and the \(n\) original records and their valid covariate names.

For every \(r\in[0,1/2]\),
\[
c\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\bigl|I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\bigr|
\le C\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r),
\]
where \(\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)\) is the prescribed effect-radius slice, and \(J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\) is the infimum of the worst-case expected length on that slice over \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\). The same constants apply to every admissible engine and naming policy.

In addition, for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), \(r\in[0,1/2]\), \(n\ge1\), and every \(I\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\), including procedures using an independent randomization seed,
\[
c\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}|I(\mathcal O,U)|,
\]
where \(\mathcal O\) is the original-record sample, \(U\) is the independent seed, and \(\lambda\) is its uniform law on the unit interval.

For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), the exponent difference is positive and satisfies
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)-\mathsf b(\beta)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)},
& \alpha+\beta\le1/2,\\[6pt]
\displaystyle
\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)},
& \alpha+\beta\ge1/2.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), the two displayed expressions agree.

The comparison constants and sample-size threshold may be selected as
\[
c_\star=c,\qquad C_\star=C,\qquad n_0=1.
\]
For every nonempty compact \(K\subseteq\mathcal D\), these selections satisfy
\[
0<\inf_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}c_\star,
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}C_\star<\infty,
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}n_0=1.
\]

bec2712ba7837aec401fb8f5f001a6d93e90733d.title: Exact smooth calibration branches
bec2712ba7837aec401fb8f5f001a6d93e90733d.body:
There exist constants \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(M>0\) with the following properties. Expectations below are over two independent fair signs, and
\[
Z_u=s_1\cos(\pi u/2)+s_2\sin(\pi u/2),
\qquad
E F(s_1,s_2)=\frac14\sum_{s_1,s_2\in\{-1,1\}}F(s_1,s_2).
\]
The covariance adjustment \(\mathfrak c\) and its normalized extension \(\mathfrak B\) are given by
\[
\begin{gathered}
d=e^t-1,\qquad
v_*=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon),\qquad
L_*=1+d\{\xi(1-\upsilon)+(1-\xi)\upsilon\},\\
D(t)=\int_0^1 e^{rt}\,dr,\\
\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2d v_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},
\qquad
\mathfrak B(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2D(t)v_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
The mixed root \(\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\) is selected from the roots in \((3/4,5/4)\) of
\[
16E\mathfrak B
 \bigl(32\eta\zeta,\tfrac12-\eta qZ_u,\tfrac12+\zeta Z_u\bigr)-q=0,
\]
with value \(1\) when that bracket contains no root. The fair root
\(\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\) is selected from the roots in \((3/10,1/2)\) of
\(\mathfrak H(t,\delta,p,u)=0\), with value \(2/5\) when that bracket contains no root. Here \(\mathfrak H\) is the smoothly extended normalized fair-matching residual, whose defining identity away from the axes is displayed below.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive odds tables.)}
For every \(t,\xi,\upsilon\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
|t|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
|\xi-\tfrac12|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
|\upsilon-\tfrac12|\le\varepsilon,
\]
put \(c=\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)\). The four cells
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{11}&=\xi\upsilon+c,&
p_{10}&=\xi(1-\upsilon)-c,\\
p_{01}&=(1-\xi)\upsilon-c,&
p_{00}&=(1-\xi)(1-\upsilon)+c
\end{aligned}
\]
are strictly positive and satisfy
\[
p_{11}+p_{10}=\xi,\qquad
p_{11}+p_{01}=\upsilon,\qquad
p_{11}+p_{10}+p_{01}+p_{00}=1,\qquad
\frac{p_{11}p_{00}}{p_{10}p_{01}}=e^t.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\mathfrak B(t,\xi,\upsilon)=\frac{\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)}{t}
\quad(t\ne0),\qquad
\mathfrak B(0,\xi,\upsilon)=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon).
\]

\item \textbf{(Signed mixed calibration.)}
For every \(|\eta|\le\varepsilon\), \(|\zeta|\le\varepsilon\), and \(u\in[0,1]\), put
\(q=\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\). Then
\[
\frac34<q<\frac54,\qquad
16E\mathfrak B
 \bigl(32\eta\zeta,\tfrac12-\eta qZ_u,\tfrac12+\zeta Z_u\bigr)-q=0,
\]
and
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,0)=\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,1),\\
E\mathfrak c
 \bigl(32\eta\zeta,\tfrac12-\eta qZ_u,\tfrac12+\zeta Z_u\bigr)
 =2\eta\zeta q,\\
\mathfrak q(-\eta,\zeta,u)=q,\qquad
\mathfrak q(\eta,-\zeta,u)=q,\\
\mathfrak q(0,\zeta,u)=1-4\zeta^2,\qquad
\mathfrak q(\eta,0,u)+4\eta^2\mathfrak q(\eta,0,u)^2=1.
\end{gathered}
\]

\item \textbf{(Fair calibration and separation.)}
For every \(t\in[0,1/4]\), \(|\delta|\le\varepsilon\), and \(u\in[0,1]\), put
\(p=\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\). Then
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathfrak p(t,\delta,0)=\mathfrak p(t,\delta,1)=\frac25,\qquad
\mathfrak p(t,0,u)=\mathfrak p(0,\delta,u)=\frac25,\\
\mathfrak p(t,-\delta,u)=p,\qquad
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,p,u)=0,\\
E\mathsf G(t,p+\delta Z_u)=\mathsf G(\mathsf T(t,\delta),p).
\end{gathered}
\]
For \(t\delta\ne0\), the residual at the selected root agrees with the unnormalized fair-matching numerator divided by \(t\delta^2\). Furthermore,
\[
|p-\tfrac25|+|\partial_u\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)|\le M\delta^2,
\]
and
\[
3t\delta^2\le t-\mathsf T(t,\delta)\le6t\delta^2,\qquad
\frac t2\le\mathsf T(t,\delta)\le t.
\]

\item \textbf{(Smooth neighborhoods and derivative bounds.)}
Both roots and every fully substituted local four-cell formula of the mixed and fair families are \(C^\infty\) on their respective closed parameter regions
\[
\begin{gathered}
|\eta|\le\varepsilon,\quad |\zeta|\le\varepsilon,\quad u\in[0,1],\\
t\in[0,1/4],\quad |\delta|\le\varepsilon,\quad u\in[0,1].
\end{gathered}
\]
For every integer \(m\ge0\), there is a constant \(B>0\) such that the norm of the \(m\)th total derivative of each root and each fully substituted local four-cell formula is at most \(B\) throughout its respective closed parameter region, uniformly over all family indices, auxiliary signs, and binary cell indices.

There also exist signed amplitude radii
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}>\varepsilon\) and
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}}>\varepsilon\), a fixed fair-root bracket half-width
\(0<b<1/10\), and open sets \(U,V\subset\mathbb R^3\) containing, respectively,
\[
\begin{gathered}
\{(\eta,\zeta,u):|\eta|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},
                       \ |\zeta|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\ u\in[0,1]\},\\
\{(t,\delta,u):t\in[0,1/4],\
                  |\delta|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}},\ u\in[0,1]\}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Throughout \(U\), the selected mixed branch is the unique zero in its fixed bracket \((3/4,5/4)\); throughout \(V\), the selected fair branch is the unique zero in the fixed centered bracket \((2/5-b,2/5+b)\). Both roots and every fully substituted local four-cell formula are \(C^\infty\) on the corresponding open set.

Finally, there is an open set \(W\subset\mathbb R^4\) containing
\[
\{(t,\delta,\xi,u):t\in[0,1/4],\
 |\delta|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}},\
 \xi\in(2/5-b,2/5+b),\ u\in[0,1]\}
\]
on which \(\mathfrak H\) is \(C^\infty\). Throughout this displayed core, for every margin \(\xi\) in the centered bracket and whenever \(t\delta\ne0\),
\[
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)
=\frac{E\mathsf G(t,\xi+\delta Z_u)-\mathsf G(\mathsf T(t,\delta),\xi)}
       {t\delta^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

06f0f876a12cb6198810091203150c019c0b61b6.title: Uniform calibrated support and smoothness
06f0f876a12cb6198810091203150c019c0b61b6.body:
There exist jointly chosen absolute constants \(\varepsilon\), the calibration radius, and \(M\), the derivative bound, satisfying
\[
0<\varepsilon\le \frac{1}{100},
\qquad M\ge 1,
\]
with the following properties. In each property, \(k\ge1\) is an integer and \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}\) is a sign vector.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Mixed membership and effects.)}
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), the prescribed domain of public smoothness exponents, set
\[
\eta=\varepsilon k^{-\alpha},
\qquad
\zeta=\varepsilon k^{-\beta}.
\]
The calibrated mixed laws \(P_{0,\sigma}\) and \(P_{1,\sigma}\) at these amplitudes belong to \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), the prescribed uniform-design homogeneous logistic model, and their homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficients satisfy
\[
\theta(P_{0,\sigma})=0,
\qquad
\theta(P_{1,\sigma})=32\eta\zeta.
\]
For each treatment label, outcome label, and covariate \(x\), the sums over all sign vectors of the corresponding conditional cell probabilities under the two mixed laws are equal.

\item \textbf{(Fair membership and effects.)}
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), set
\[
\delta=\varepsilon k^{-\beta}.
\]
For every \(t\in[0,1/4]\), the fair random law \(P_{t,\sigma}\) and the deterministic fair comparator \(P_{*,t,\delta}\) belong to \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), and
\[
\theta(P_{t,\sigma})=t,
\qquad
\theta(P_{*,t,\delta})=\mathsf T(t,\delta),
\]
where \(\mathsf T(t,\delta)\) is the calibrated comparator effect. For each treatment label, outcome label, and covariate \(x\), the uniform average over the \(2^{k+1}\) sign vectors of the conditional cell probability under \(P_{t,\sigma}\) equals the corresponding comparator cell probability.

\item \textbf{(Signed validity and derivative bounds.)}
For all signed amplitudes satisfying
\[
|\eta|\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
|\zeta|\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
|\delta|\le\varepsilon,
\]
the conditional four-cell tables of both mixed branches are valid probability tables, as are those of both fair branches for every \(t\in[0,1/4]\). For every sign vector, treatment label, outcome label, and covariate \(x\), their one-record densities relative to uniform four-label measure lie in \([1/2,2]\). The mixed densities, viewed as functions of \((\eta,\zeta)\), and the fair densities, viewed as functions of \(\delta\) with \(t\) fixed, are twice continuously differentiable at every point of the corresponding closed amplitude box. The norms of their first and second total amplitude derivatives are at most \(M\), uniformly over all these indices and amplitudes. This includes the mixed second derivative in \(\eta\) and \(\zeta\) and the deterministic comparator's derivatives in \(\delta\).

\item \textbf{(Common smooth neighborhoods.)}
There exists an open subset of \(\mathbb R^2\) containing
\[
\{(\eta,\zeta):|\eta|\le\varepsilon,\ |\zeta|\le\varepsilon\}
\]
on which every mixed density is infinitely continuously differentiable in its amplitude arguments. There also exists an open subset of \(\mathbb R\) containing
\[
[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]
\]
on which every fair density is infinitely continuously differentiable in \(\delta\). Each neighborhood is common to every integer \(k\ge1\), sign vector, branch, treatment label, outcome label, and covariate \(x\); the fair neighborhood is also common to every \(t\in[0,1/4]\).

\item \textbf{(Signed singleton matching.)}
Throughout the same signed closed amplitude boxes, for each treatment label, outcome label, and covariate \(x\), the sums over all sign vectors of the conditional cell probabilities under the two mixed laws are equal. For every \(t\in[0,1/4]\), the uniform average over all \(2^{k+1}\) sign vectors of each conditional cell probability under the fair random law equals the corresponding cell probability under the deterministic fair comparator.
\end{itemize}

632473d1f821664f6a077c98857520139f166cd5.title: Original-record mixture bounds
632473d1f821664f6a077c98857520139f166cd5.body:
Let \(\varepsilon\) and \(M\) be the radius and envelope constant selected from the fixed joint calibrated-support certificate, with \(0<\varepsilon\le 1/100\) and \(M\ge 1\). Define the positive constants
\[
\kappa=\frac{1}{96\exp(1)},
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{mix}}=96\exp(2)\,8^2M^4.
\]
For sample laws \(Q,Q'\), use the unhalved squared Hellinger distance
\[
\mathcal H^2(Q,Q')
=
\int
\left(
\sqrt{\frac{dQ}{dR}}-
\sqrt{\frac{dQ'}{dR}}
\right)^2\,dR,
\]
where \(R\) is the original-record sample reference measure.

For every choice satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample and partition sizes.)} \(n,k\) are integers with \(n\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Occupancy.)} \(n/k\le\kappa\).
\item \textbf{(Signed amplitudes.)} \(\eta,\zeta,\delta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
|\eta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
|\zeta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
|\delta|\le\varepsilon,
\]
\end{itemize}
let \(Q_b\), for \(b\in\{0,1\}\), and \(Q_t\) be the uniform finite mixtures of the calibrated mixed and fair original-record sample laws, respectively:
\[
Q_b=\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[P_{b,\sigma}^{\otimes n}\right],
\qquad
Q_t=\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[P_{t,\sigma}^{\otimes n}\right],
\]
where the expectation averages uniformly over the finite sign vectors. Let \(P_{*,t,\delta}\) be the deterministic fair comparator obtained from the fair construction at partition size \(k\), center \(t\), and amplitude \(\delta\), using the identically false sign vector. Then
\[
\mathcal H^2(Q_0,Q_1)
\le
C_{\mathrm{mix}}\frac{n^2}{k}\eta^2\zeta^2,
\]
and, for every \(t\in[0,1/4]\),
\[
\mathcal H^2\!\left(Q_t,P_{*,t,\delta}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{mix}}\frac{n^2}{k}\delta^4.
\]

96d3b70b3cbda0c1eb1b623b6b05f423a9bdd604.title: Admissibility of the concrete engine
96d3b70b3cbda0c1eb1b623b6b05f423a9bdd604.body: The explicit rational arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E_0\), consisting of the Machin enclosure for \(\pi\), the cosine interval routine, and the endpoint extensions of the scalar exponential, logarithm, square-root, and integer-base power routines, satisfies all primitive admissibility contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine}.

d9c0d4135cfa37e0f6283249bebc2cf3d6219d43.title: Fixed-budget interval realization
d9c0d4135cfa37e0f6283249bebc2cf3d6219d43.body:
The dyadic-floor naming policy \(\mathsf N_0\) is admissible in the sense of \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}. Fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Engine.)} An admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\), satisfying its primitive contracts.
\item \textbf{(Names.)} An admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\) as in \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}.
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} An integer \(n\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Exponents.)} Public exponents \((\alpha,\beta)\) in the domain
\[
\mathcal D=\{(\alpha,\beta):0<\beta<1/4,\ \beta<\alpha\le 1\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
For every tuple \(\mathcal O\in\Omega^n\) of observed records, where
\(\Omega=[0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), the following guarantees hold.

At the public rank budget
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,
\]
the rank computation returns rational target enclosures
\([a_C,b_C]\) and \([a_S,b_S]\), each of width at most one. Here \(b_C,b_S\) denote the upper endpoints of the rank enclosures. With the targets and selected ranks of \cref{obj:def:resolutions},
\[
R_C=n^{2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)},\qquad
R_S=n^{2/(4\beta+1)},\qquad
k_C=\max\{\lceil b_C\rceil,0\},\qquad
k_S=\max\{\lceil b_S\rceil,0\},
\]
one has
\[
R_C\le k_C<R_C+2\le 3R_C,\qquad
R_S\le k_S<R_S+2\le 3R_S.
\]

For the endpoint construction, let \(\widehat C_n,\widehat S_n\) be the coordinate estimates at these retained ranks, and now use \(b_C,b_S\) for the error radii
\[
b_C=8k_C^{-(\alpha+\beta)}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_C)},\qquad
b_S=25k_S^{-2\beta}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_S)},
\]
where \(V_n(k)\) is the public variance envelope. Define
\[
c_\pm=\widehat C_n\pm b_C,\qquad
s_\pm=\operatorname{clip}_{[s_0,1]}(\widehat S_n\pm b_S),
\]
where \(s_0\) is the denominator floor and
\(\operatorname{clip}_{[l,u]}(v)=\min\{u,\max\{l,v\}\}\).
The ideal endpoints obtained from the clipped logarithmic inversion \(F(c,d)\) of the coordinate ratio are
\[
L=\min\{F(c_-,s_-),F(c_-,s_+)\},\qquad
R=\max\{F(c_+,s_-),F(c_+,s_+)\}.
\]
Here \(L,R\) denote interval endpoints.

At the public endpoint budget
\[
K=\max\{k_C,k_S\},\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)
=44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil,
\]
the endpoint computation returns rational enclosures satisfying
\[
L\in[L_-,L_+],\qquad R\in[R_-,R_+],\qquad
L_+-L_-\le \frac1n,\qquad R_+-R_-\le \frac1n.
\]
The literal output \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O)\) is a nonempty rational closed connected interval contained in \([-1/2,1/2]\), and
\[
[L,R]\subseteq
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O),
\qquad
\operatorname{length}\!\left(
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O)
\right)
\le R-L+\frac2n.
\]
For each fixed admissible engine, naming policy, sample size, and exponent pair, the output map from \(\Omega^n\) to the space \(\mathcal C\) of admissible effect intervals is Borel measurable.

dd58087f82fe5b9703794619d0d5f959d37df177.title: Full honest frontier and attainment
dd58087f82fe5b9703794619d0d5f959d37df177.body:
Let the domain of public exponents be
\[
\mathcal D=\{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R^2:0<\beta<1/4,\ \beta<\alpha\le1\}.
\]
For \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), define the numerator and denominator exponents and the expected-length profile by
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)
=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},
\qquad
\mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1},
\qquad
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}+r n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)}.
\]
There exist absolute constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c\) and \(0<C\), for which all the following statements hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Universal attainment.)}
For every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\), every admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\), every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), and every integer \(n\ge1\), set
\[
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta).
\]
This literal output of the fixed-budget represented construction belongs to
\(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\) as defined in
\cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. It receives the public exponents, the original records, and the independent randomization seed, and terminates on every valid named input within the prescribed rank and endpoint precision budgets. For every sample and seed, its output is a nonempty rational closed interval: there exist \(l,u\in\mathbb Q\) such that
\[
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)
=[l,u],
\qquad
-\frac12\le l\le u\le\frac12.
\]
For every \(r\in[0,1/2]\), the minimax expected length from
\cref{obj:def:length-objective} satisfies
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\left|I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\right|
\le C\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]
The same constants apply to every admissible engine and naming policy.

\item \textbf{(Concrete sequence.)}
Take \(\mathsf E_0\) to be the explicit concrete arithmetic engine and
\(\mathsf N_0\) to be the dyadic-floor naming policy, and define
\[
I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)
=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0}(\alpha,\beta).
\]
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\) and every integer \(n\ge1\),
\(I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\). For every sample and seed, there exist \(l,u\in\mathbb Q\) such that
\[
I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)=[l,u],
\qquad
-\frac12\le l\le u\le\frac12.
\]
For every \(r\in[0,1/2]\),
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\left|I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\right|
\le C\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]

\item \textbf{(Universal lower bound.)}
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every \(r\in[0,1/2]\), every integer \(n\ge1\), and every
\(I\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\), including procedures using an independent randomization seed,
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}|I(\mathcal O,U)|.
\]

\item \textbf{(Elbow identities.)}
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\),
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)-\mathsf b(\beta)>0,
\]
and
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)-\mathsf b(\beta)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)},
& \alpha+\beta\le1/2,\\[6pt]
\displaystyle
\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)},
& \alpha+\beta\ge1/2.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), the two expressions agree:
\[
\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)}
=
\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Compact uniformity.)}
Choose the comparison constants and sample-size threshold as
\[
c_\star(\alpha,\beta)=c,\qquad
C_\star(\alpha,\beta)=C,\qquad
n_0(\alpha,\beta)=1.
\]
For every nonempty compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal D\),
\[
0<
\inf_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal K}c_\star(\alpha,\beta),
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal K}C_\star(\alpha,\beta)<\infty,
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal K}n_0(\alpha,\beta)=1.
\]
\end{itemize}

e15be66979f53e3d0cc75c7472d898c97b665f89.title: The full honest frontier
e15be66979f53e3d0cc75c7472d898c97b665f89.body:
There exist absolute constants \(c,C\in(0,\infty)\) with the following properties. The public exponent domain and the two rate exponents are
\[
\mathcal D=\{(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb R^2:0<\beta<1/4,\ \beta<\alpha\le1\},
\qquad
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)=
\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},
\qquad
\mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1}.
\]
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every integer \(n\ge1\), and every \(r\in[0,1/2]\), the sharp expected-length profile is
\[
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}+r n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)}.
\]

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Concrete attainment.)}
Let
\[
I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)
=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0}(\alpha,\beta),
\]
where \(\mathsf E_0\) is the concrete certified arithmetic engine and \(\mathsf N_0\) is the dyadic-floor naming policy. This radius-independent procedure belongs to \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}. For every sample and randomization seed, its output has the form
\[
I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)=[l,u],
\qquad
l,u\in\mathbb Q,\qquad -\frac12\le l\le u\le\frac12.
\]
With \(J_n\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:length-objective},
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\bigl|I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\bigr|
\le C\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]

\item \textbf{(Universal construction.)}
For every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and every admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\), the procedure
\(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\)
is Borel and globally \(90\%\)-honest. It terminates within the prescribed fixed budgets on every valid named input, receives the data and public inputs, and returns a nonempty closed interval with rational endpoints in \([-1/2,1/2]\). The same constants satisfy
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\bigl|I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}
(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\bigr|
\le C\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]

\item \textbf{(Uniform constants.)}
Take \(c_\star=c\), \(C_\star=C\), and \(n_0=1\). For every nonempty compact subset \(K\subseteq\mathcal D\),
\[
0<\inf_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}c_\star,
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}C_\star<\infty,
\qquad
\sup_{(\alpha,\beta)\in K}n_0=1.
\]

\item \textbf{(Elbow identities.)}
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\),
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)-\mathsf b(\beta)>0,
\qquad
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)-\mathsf b(\beta)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)},
&\alpha+\beta\le\frac12,\\[6pt]
\displaystyle
\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)},
&\alpha+\beta\ge\frac12.
\end{cases}
\]
At \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), the two expressions agree:
\[
\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)}
=
\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Universal converse.)}
For every \(I\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\), including procedures using independent randomization,
\[
c\,\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}|I(\mathcal O,U)|.
\]
\end{itemize}

591898414159264e6c8ceab6e1966bd645423f7e.title: Uniform covariate design
591898414159264e6c8ceab6e1966bd645423f7e.body:
The covariate \(X\) has the uniform probability law \(\lambda\) on the unit interval under the observed law \(P\):
\[
P\circ X^{-1}=\lambda.
\]

0163ededfae8fe571163191f8cdd6d5302613776.title: Homogeneous conditional log-odds relation
0163ededfae8fe571163191f8cdd6d5302613776.body:
The treated-arm conditional outcome risk \(\mu_1(P,x)\) satisfies
\[
\mu_1(P,x)=\ell\{\nu(P,x)+\theta(P)\}
\qquad (x\in[0,1]),
\]
where \(\ell\) is the logistic map, \(\nu(P,x)\) is the native prognosis logit, and \(\theta(P)\) is the homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient.

19bf6da6b8d742004bae72f9978c65a7bac3ddb5.title: Homogeneous effect envelope
19bf6da6b8d742004bae72f9978c65a7bac3ddb5.body:
The homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient \(\theta(P)\) satisfies
\[
|\theta(P)|\le \frac12.
\]

1133788ee53222a28bf76a54cb7f2e9ad19e919a.title: Propensity Hölder seminorm bound
1133788ee53222a28bf76a54cb7f2e9ad19e919a.body:
The Hölder seminorm of the native propensity-logit function \(g(P,\cdot)\) at the public smoothness exponent \(\alpha\) satisfies
\[
[g(P,\cdot)]_\alpha\le 2.
\]

25038d0b681707526281b12c178b30b2421c3967.title: Prognosis Hölder bound
25038d0b681707526281b12c178b30b2421c3967.body:
The native prognosis-logit function \(\nu(P,\cdot)\) satisfies the Hölder seminorm bound
\[
[\nu(P,\cdot)]_\beta\le 2.
\]

c4f9a6407f7e1f705c497a7499b311388aa7c132.title: Effect evaluation radius
c4f9a6407f7e1f705c497a7499b311388aa7c132.body:
The homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient \(\theta(P)\) satisfies
\[
|\theta(P)|\le r.
\]

a18f7c8f110a9ca35e3ef2c20788954023b8ca21.title: Global interval coverage
a18f7c8f110a9ca35e3ef2c20788954023b8ca21.body:
The interval procedure \(I(\mathcal O,U)\), evaluated on the tuple of observed records \(\mathcal O\) and an independent uniform randomization seed \(U\), satisfies
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)}
(P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda)
\{\theta(P)\in I(\mathcal O,U)\}\ge 0.90,
\]
where \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\) is the ambient observed-law model, \(\lambda\) is the uniform probability law on the unit interval, and \(\theta(P)\) is the homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient.

077fb27004647278b76372c45e2292098548ce07.title: Homogeneous logistic class \(\mathcal L\)
077fb27004647278b76372c45e2292098548ce07.body:
\[
\mathcal L
=
\left\{
P:\mu_1(P,x)=\ell\{\nu(P,x)+\theta(P)\}
\ \text{for every }x\in[0,1]
\right\}.
\]
Here \(\mu_1(P,x)\) is the treated-arm conditional outcome risk, \(\ell\) is the logistic map, \(\nu(P,x)\) is the native prognosis logit, and \(\theta(P)\) is the homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient. The defining relation is that of \cref{obj:ass:homogeneous-logit}.

0152d248d69036c1d771f3e18f9c8ccacafe3e20.title: Ambient model \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\)
0152d248d69036c1d771f3e18f9c8ccacafe3e20.body:
\(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\) is the class of observed laws \(P\) satisfying the following conditions, for each \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), the prescribed domain of public smoothness exponents:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Uniform design.)} With \(\lambda\) denoting the uniform probability law on the unit interval,
\[
P\circ X^{-1}=\lambda.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:uniform-design}.
\item \textbf{(Homogeneous logit.)} The treated-arm conditional outcome risk \(\mu_1(P,x)\), logistic map \(\ell\), native prognosis logit \(\nu(P,x)\), and homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient \(\theta(P)\) satisfy
\[
\mu_1(P,x)=\ell\{\nu(P,x)+\theta(P)\}
\qquad (x\in[0,1]).
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:homogeneous-logit}.
\item \textbf{(Effect envelope.)}
\[
|\theta(P)|\le \frac12.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:effect-envelope}.
\item \textbf{(Propensity envelope.)} The native propensity-logit function \(g(P,\cdot)\) satisfies
\[
\|g(P,\cdot)\|_\infty\le 1.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:propensity-envelope}.
\item \textbf{(Propensity smoothness.)}
\[
[g(P,\cdot)]_\alpha\le 2.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:propensity-holder}.
\item \textbf{(Prognosis envelope.)}
\[
\|\nu(P,\cdot)\|_\infty\le 1.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:prognosis-envelope}.
\item \textbf{(Prognosis smoothness.)}
\[
[\nu(P,\cdot)]_\beta\le 2.
\]
See \cref{obj:ass:prognosis-holder}.
\end{itemize}
The bracket notation denotes the Hölder seminorm at the indicated public exponent.

6d6d4a1421bed48dc4cdc375fddab293243ed2ea.title: Effect-radius slice \(\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)\)
6d6d4a1421bed48dc4cdc375fddab293243ed2ea.body:
\[
\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)
=
\{P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta):|\theta(P)|\le r\}
\qquad
\bigl((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D,\ r\in[0,1/2]\bigr).
\]
Here \(\mathcal D\) is the prescribed domain of public smoothness exponents and \(\theta(P)\) is the homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient. This defines the slice of the ambient model in \cref{obj:def:model} satisfying \cref{obj:ass:evaluation-radius}.

a70267e5924289a9857700e96e065e4140fbf693.title: Honest interval procedures $\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)$
a70267e5924289a9857700e96e065e4140fbf693.body:
For every \(n\ge1\) and \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), define
\[
\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)
=
\left\{
I:\Omega^n\times[0,1]\to\mathcal C:
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)}
(P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda)
\{\theta(P)\in I(\mathcal O,U)\}
\ge0.90
\right\},
\]
where the maps \(I\) are Borel and have measurable coverage events and interval length, as required by \cref{obj:ass:global-coverage}. Here \(\Omega\) is the measurable space of one observed record, \(\mathcal O\) is the tuple of original observed records, \(\mathcal C\) is the space of admissible nonempty connected Borel effect intervals, and \(\lambda\) is the uniform probability law on \([0,1]\). The variable \(U\) is an independent randomization seed, \(\mathcal D\) is the prescribed domain of public smoothness exponents, and \(\theta(P)\) is the homogeneous conditional log-odds coefficient.

5142a4b46262ae86cacfd9b90aa4b1a3d172d0c2.title: Minimax expected length $J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)$

0626e98751ee44c4c83390bed911e4545829c07c.title: Full-data law $\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}$
0626e98751ee44c4c83390bed911e4545829c07c.body:
The full-data law \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) is defined by the successive draws
\[
X\sim\lambda,\qquad
(Y^0,Y^1)\mid X=x\sim\Gamma(P,x),\qquad
A\mid(X,Y^0,Y^1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\{e(P,X)\},
\]
and the observed outcome
\[
Y=(1-A)Y^0+AY^1.
\]
Here \(\lambda\) is the uniform probability law on \([0,1]\), \(Y^0\) and \(Y^1\) are the control and treated potential outcomes, \(\Gamma(P,x)\) is an admissible conditional coupling of these outcomes, and \(e(P,X)\) is the treatment probability conditional on the covariate under the observed law \(P\).

4d7b0886cda10ab8084e0404f288c24ed4c29f8b.title: Projection statistic $\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)$
4d7b0886cda10ab8084e0404f288c24ed4c29f8b.body:
For \(n\ge2\), the ordered-pair projection statistic for two bounded record marks \(W\) and \(V\) is
\[
\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)
=
\frac{1}{n(n-1)}
\sum_{\substack{1\le i,j\le n\\ i\ne j}}
H_k(X_i,X_j)W(O_i)V(O_j).
\]
Here \(O_i\) is the \(i\)th observed record, \(X_i\) is its covariate, and \(H_k\) is the kernel of the projection at rank \(k\).

222814d9aebbe0a7bfa45834ff65ff2aea89d274.title: Projection ranks $k_C$ and $k_S$
222814d9aebbe0a7bfa45834ff65ff2aea89d274.body:
The inputs are \(n\ge2\), the public smoothness exponents \(\alpha,\beta\), a fixed admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\), and a Borel policy \(\mathsf N\) selecting valid representations of the public exponents.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the public precision budget and the target resolutions to
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad
R_C=n^{2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)},\qquad
R_S=n^{2/(4\beta+1)}.
\]
For each positive integer \(b\), the integer logarithm is computed by comparisons using
\[
\lceil\log_2 b\rceil
=
\min\{q\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}:2^q\ge b\}.
\]
Here \(b\) denotes the integer argument of this computation.

\item At precision \(q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)\), obtain the rational enclosures of the exponents supplied under \(\mathsf N\) and intersect them with \([0,1]\) for \(\alpha\) and \([0,1/4]\) for \(\beta\). Compute the ranges of the exponents in the two target powers by exact rational range operations, then apply the positive-integer-base power operation of \(\mathsf E\) at the same precision. Denote the resulting rational enclosures by
\[
R_C\in[a_C,b_C],\qquad
R_S\in[a_S,b_S].
\]
In this construction, \(b_C\) and \(b_S\) denote upper endpoints of resolution enclosures.

\item Output the integer ranks
\[
k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_C\rceil,\qquad
k_S(n,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_S\rceil.
\]
These ranks are fixed before sampling: \(\mathsf E\) is fixed, and the exponent representations selected by \(\mathsf N\) depend only on the public exponents. Different admissible engines or representations may produce different integers.
\end{enumerate}

81527531b26e70bba1aa9c9de46514ce471e88f7.title: Coordinate estimates $\widehat C_n$ and $\widehat S_n$
81527531b26e70bba1aa9c9de46514ce471e88f7.body:
For \(n\ge2\), define the exact real sample coordinates by
\[
\widehat C_n
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n A_iY_i
-
\mathbb U_{n,k_C}(A,Y),
\qquad
\widehat S_n
=
\mathbb U_{n,k_S}\bigl(A(1-Y),(1-A)Y\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathbb U_{n,k}\) is the ordered-pair projection statistic and the retained ranks are
\[
k_C=k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N),
\qquad
k_S=k_S(n,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N).
\]
Both ranks are selected by the fixed-budget resolution construction using the same admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and the public exponent representations selected by the Borel policy \(\mathsf N\). The upper construction uses this same engine and these retained ranks to enclose the finite sums from the supplied covariate representations. The statistics \(\widehat C_n\) and \(\widehat S_n\) estimate \(C(P)\) and \(S(P)\), respectively, the observable numerator and denominator coordinates in the odds identity.

b70cfed9f4dd6e86c29dc25b08b0dd7bdff4307e.title: Arithmetic engine $\mathsf E$
b70cfed9f4dd6e86c29dc25b08b0dd7bdff4307e.body:
An arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) is a deterministic collection of maps on closed rational intervals, with integer precision input \(q\ge 0\) and tolerance
\[
\epsilon_q=2^{-q}.
\]
It supplies rational enclosures of \(\pi\), the exponential and cosine on every bounded rational interval, the logarithm on rational intervals \([a,b]\) with \(0<a\le b\), the square root on rational intervals \([a,b]\) with \(0\le a\le b\), and the power \(b^v\) for a positive integer base \(b\) and a rational exponent interval contained in \([-3,3]\). The symbols \(a,b,v,q\) are bound primitive arguments; in the power primitive, \(b\) denotes the integer base, supplied separately from the interval endpoints.

The engine also supplies exact rational range operations for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division on denominator intervals avoiding zero, minimum, maximum, intersection, and clipping. In particular, the minimum of two intervals has range
\[
\min\bigl([a,b],[c,d]\bigr)
=
[\min(a,c),\min(b,d)],
\]
and multiplication has range
\[
[a,b]\,[c,d]
=
[\min\{ac,ad,bc,bd\},\max\{ac,ad,bc,bd\}].
\]
Division uses the reciprocal range followed by multiplication, and clipping uses the exact minimum and maximum operations.

Admissibility requires the following primitive contracts.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Enclosure.)} Every returned interval contains the real image of its input interval.
\item \textbf{(Monotone primitives.)} For exponential, logarithm, square root, and positive-integer-base power, each returned endpoint differs outward from the corresponding exact range endpoint by at most \(\epsilon_q\).
\item \textbf{(Constant enclosure.)} The returned enclosure of \(\pi\) lies in \([3,4]\), with outward excess at each endpoint at most \(\epsilon_q\).
\item \textbf{(Cosine.)} At the rational midpoint of the input interval, the engine encloses the cosine value with outward endpoint excess at most \(\epsilon_q\). It enlarges this enclosure by half the input width on each side and intersects the result with \([-1,1]\). The returned width is at most the input width plus \(2\epsilon_q\).
\item \textbf{(Primitive domains and signs.)} Exponential and power outputs have positive lower endpoints, and square-root outputs have nonnegative lower endpoints. Logarithm is evaluated on intervals with positive rational lower endpoints, and division is evaluated on denominator intervals avoiding zero.
\item \textbf{(Finite rational computation.)} Every map is defined by a finite rational recurrence whose iteration count is bounded by a specified public integer function of the rational range bounds, the integer base when present, and \(q\). The recurrence may use rational comparisons and integer arithmetic; its access to a real input is exclusively through the supplied rational interval.
\item \textbf{(Independent choice.)} The engine is fixed independently of all public exponents, sample sizes, observed records, laws, naming policies, evaluation radii, and unknown nuisance quantities.
\end{itemize}
Distinct admissible engines may return distinct rational enclosures. Admissibility is specified entirely by these primitive contracts, with rank conclusions, final-endpoint conclusions, final precision budgets, and statistical properties outside its defining requirements.

e03c781dad63ec8f6378ca79d38ac9be56e1a307.title: Diagnostic envelope \(d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\)
e03c781dad63ec8f6378ca79d38ac9be56e1a307.body:
The diagnostic envelope is
\[
d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=
n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}
+r\,n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)},
\]
where the numerator and denominator rate exponents are, respectively,
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)
=
\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},
\qquad
\mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1}.
\]

c6d2f6428b215478a6603d6cfb8e21820f916ac3.title: Rational interval \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\)
c6d2f6428b215478a6603d6cfb8e21820f916ac3.body:
The interval procedure takes the sample size \(n\), public exponents \(\alpha,\beta\), and observed sample \(\mathcal O\), with an independently fixed admissible rational arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and a Borel policy \(\mathsf N\) supplying valid dyadic interval representations of the exponents and observed covariates.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(n=1\), return
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{1,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=[-1/2,1/2].
\]
For \(n\ge2\), continue with the following steps.

\item Select the numerator and denominator projection ranks at the fixed public rank precision:
\[
k_C=k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N),
\qquad
k_S=k_S(n,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N).
\]
Retain these same integers in the coordinate estimates \(\widehat C_n\) and \(\widehat S_n\).

\item Define the smoothness sum, variance envelope, and coordinate error radii by
\[
s=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
V_n(k)=\frac{10}{n}+\frac{4k}{n(n-1)},
\]
\[
b_C=8k_C^{-s}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_C)},
\qquad
b_S=25k_S^{-2\beta}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_S)}.
\]
Here \(b_C,b_S\) denote error radii; their local meanings in resolution enclosures are enclosure endpoints.

\item Define scalar clipping, the confidence-rectangle endpoints, and the inversion map by
\[
\operatorname{clip}_{[l,u]}(v)=\max\{l,\min\{u,v\}\},
\]
\[
c_\pm=\widehat C_n\pm b_C,\qquad
s_\pm=\operatorname{clip}_{[s_0,1]}(\widehat S_n\pm b_S),
\]
\[
F(c,d)=
\log\left(
\operatorname{clip}_{[\exp(-1/2),\exp(1/2)]}
\left(1+\frac{c}{d}\right)
\right),
\]
where \(s_0\) is the uniform positive lower bound for the denominator coordinate. The ideal interval endpoints are
\[
L=\min\{F(c_-,s_-),F(c_-,s_+)\},
\qquad
R=\max\{F(c_+,s_-),F(c_+,s_+)\}.
\]
Here \(R\) denotes the upper endpoint; in the resolution construction it locally denotes a rank target.

\item Define the endpoint precision budget by
\[
K=\max\{k_C,k_S\},
\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)
=
44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil
+4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil.
\]
At this precision, query the supplied dyadic interval representations of both exponents and all observed covariates. Evaluate the displayed finite expressions with the same engine \(\mathsf E\), its primitive maps, and exact rational range operations in the displayed expression tree, retaining \(k_C,k_S\). The resulting rational endpoint enclosures satisfy
\[
L_-\le L\le L_+,\qquad
R_-\le R\le R_+,
\]
\[
L_+-L_-\le\frac1n,\qquad
R_+-R_-\le\frac1n.
\]
Evaluation terminates after the fixed rank and endpoint budgets on every valid input.

\item Output the nonempty closed rational interval
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=
[\max\{-1/2,L_-\},\ \min\{1/2,R_+\}].
\]
It contains the ideal interval and has at most \(2/n\) additional length:
\[
[L,R]\subseteq I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta),
\qquad
0\le
\operatorname{length}\!\left(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\right)
-(R-L)
\le\frac2n.
\]
\end{enumerate}
The procedure uses the public exponents, observed sample, selected dyadic representations, and fixed engine. Its rational endpoints may vary with the admissible engine and valid representations.

663000c996745ce99798bf3d6d373dab5e643328.title: Frontier pair \(\operatorname{frontierHandle}(\mathsf E,\mathsf N)\)
663000c996745ce99798bf3d6d373dab5e643328.body:
The frontier pair and its attaining interval family are
\[
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r),
\qquad
\operatorname{frontierHandle}(\mathsf E,\mathsf N)
=
\bigl(\rho,I^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\bigr),
\]
\[
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}
=
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N},
\]
for every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible naming policy \(\mathsf N\). Here \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\) denotes the procedure sequence for this fixed engine and policy. The concrete sequence is
\[
I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0},
\]
where \(\mathsf E_0\) is the explicit rational arithmetic engine and \(\mathsf N_0\) is the dyadic-floor naming policy.

Write \(c_\star\), \(C_\star\), and \(n_0\) for the lower comparison constant, upper comparison constant, and sample-size threshold selected in the sharp comparison, respectively.

Each interval is the literal rational output of the fixed-budget expression tree evaluated with the supplied fixed engine and valid dyadic interval representations. Different engines or representations may yield different rational intervals satisfying the endpoint enclosure bounds. Every member uses the observed-law coordinates \((C,S)\), separate projection resolutions, and joint inversion. Its represented inputs are \((n,\alpha,\beta,\mathcal O)\), with representations selected by \(\mathsf N\) and independently fixed engine \(\mathsf E\); the radius \(r\) indexes the expected-length profile.

The converse uses continuous calibrated priors with admissible native propensity and prognosis perturbations, one common scalar effect per draw, analytic singleton matching, and factorization across disjoint latent-sign components conditional on the original covariates. It applies independently of the arithmetic engine and naming policy.

31498dbab76f33436d8d4765c7c8d48a9d19a7f9.title: Calibration maps \(\mathfrak c,\mathfrak B,\mathfrak q,\mathsf G,\mathsf T,\mathfrak H,\mathfrak p\)
31498dbab76f33436d8d4765c7c8d48a9d19a7f9.body:
The covariance calibration maps are
\[
\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=
\frac{2dv_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},
\qquad
\mathfrak B(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=
\frac{2D(t)v_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},
\]
where \(\xi,\upsilon\) are scalar margins near \(1/2\), and
\[
d=\exp(t)-1,\qquad
v_*=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon),
\]
\[
L_*=1+d\{\xi(1-\upsilon)+(1-\xi)\upsilon\},
\qquad
D(t)=\int_0^1\exp(st)\,ds.
\]
Here \(s\) is an integration variable. These maps are defined where the displayed square root and denominator are positive.

For independent uniform signs \(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_1\), define
\[
Z_u=\epsilon_0\cos(\pi u/2)+\epsilon_1\sin(\pi u/2),
\]
and let \(E\) denote expectation over these two signs. Fix the established mixed-calibration branch domain, with signed amplitude radius \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}>0\). For
\[
|\eta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad
|\zeta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad
u\in[0,1],
\]
the mixed-calibration map is the unique root
\[
\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\in(3/4,5/4)
\]
satisfying
\[
16E\mathfrak B
\left(32\eta\zeta,\frac12-\eta\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)Z_u,
\frac12+\zeta Z_u\right)
-\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)=0.
\]
The smaller closed amplitude squares used for support and mixture bounds lie within this branch domain.

For the separate fair-prior maps, set
\[
p_*=\frac25,\qquad v_*=p_*(1-p_*)=\frac6{25},
\]
where \(v_*\) now denotes the Bernoulli variance at the fair-branch baseline risk. Define
\[
\mathsf G(t,\xi)=
\frac{\exp(t)\xi}{1+\{\exp(t)-1\}\xi},
\qquad
B_*=1+\{\exp(t)-1\}p_*,
\]
\[
\mathsf T(t,\delta)
=
t+
\log\left(1-\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{p_*B_*}\right)
-
\log\left(1+\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{(1-p_*)B_*}\right).
\]
For \(t\delta\ne0\), define the normalized fair-matching residual by
\[
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)
=
\frac{
E\mathsf G(t,\xi+\delta Z_u)
-\mathsf G(\mathsf T(t,\delta),\xi)}
{t\delta^2}.
\]

Fix the established fair-calibration branch domain, with signed amplitude radius \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}}>0\) and sufficiently small bracket half-width \(b\in(0,1/10)\). Here \(b\) denotes the fair-root bracket half-width. The domain contains
\[
0\le t\le\frac14,\qquad
|\delta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}},\qquad
u\in[0,1],
\]
together with the fixed open neighborhood of these parameters, including signed parameters across \(t=0\) and the spatial endpoints. On this neighborhood the fair-formula denominators and logarithm arguments are positive. At \(t=0\) or \(\delta=0\), \(\mathfrak H\) is its removable smooth extension on this neighborhood.

The fair-calibration map is the unique root
\[
p_*-b<\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)<p_*+b
\]
satisfying
\[
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u),u)=0.
\]
On the established neighborhood, this is also the root selected in the bracket \((3/10,1/2)\). The smaller closed amplitude neighborhood used for support and mixture bounds lies within this fair branch domain, uniformly over \(t\in[0,1/4]\) and \(u\in[0,1]\). These definitions specify the calibration branches on their established domains of existence, uniqueness, regularity, and matching.

cd08e1657e4e266106f26caaf596bf94bb133873.title: Continuous calibrated priors \(P_{b,\sigma},P_{t,\sigma},Q_b,Q_t\)
cd08e1657e4e266106f26caaf596bf94bb133873.body:
The continuous sign field on an equal partition is
\[
\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)
=
\sigma_j\cos(\pi u/2)+\sigma_{j+1}\sin(\pi u/2),
\qquad
u=\frac{x-j\Delta}{\Delta},
\qquad
\Delta=\frac1k,
\]
for an integer \(k\ge1\), independent uniform signs
\(\sigma=(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_k)\), and
\(j\Delta\le x\le(j+1)\Delta\), \(0\le j<k\). Either adjoining cell gives the value at a shared endpoint.

For signed amplitudes \(\eta,\zeta\), define
\[
e_0(x)=\frac12+\eta\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x),
\qquad
e_1(x)=\frac12-\eta\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x),
\]
\[
m_\sigma(x)=\frac12+\zeta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x),
\qquad
c_0(x)=0,
\qquad
c_1(x)=\mathfrak c(32\eta\zeta,e_1(x),m_\sigma(x)).
\]
For the family index \(b\in\{0,1\}\), the law \(P_{b,\sigma}\) has uniform covariate law \(\lambda\) on the unit interval and conditional cell probabilities
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{11}&=e_bm_\sigma+c_b,
&
p_{10}&=e_b(1-m_\sigma)-c_b,\\
p_{01}&=(1-e_b)m_\sigma-c_b,
&
p_{00}&=(1-e_b)(1-m_\sigma)+c_b.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(e_b,m_\sigma,c_b\) are evaluated at the current covariate; \(p_{11},p_{10},p_{01},p_{00}\) correspond to treated success, treated failure, control success, and control failure.

For \(0\le t\le1/4\), the separate fair-treatment laws \(P_{t,\sigma}\) and \(P_{*,t,\delta}\) have covariate law \(\lambda\), treatment probability \(1/2\), and control and treated outcome risks
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&\mu_0(x)&\mu_1(x)\\ \hline
P_{t,\sigma}
&
\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)+\delta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)
&
\mathsf G\bigl(t,\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)+\delta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)\bigr)
\\
P_{*,t,\delta}
&
\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)
&
\mathsf G\bigl(\mathsf T(t,\delta),\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\bigr).
\end{array}
\]
These formulas define probability laws on the calibration neighborhood where the conditional cells are positive.

The sample mixtures are
\[
Q_b
=
2^{-(k+1)}
\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{k+1}}
P_{b,\sigma}^{\otimes n},
\qquad
Q_t
=
2^{-(k+1)}
\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{k+1}}
P_{t,\sigma}^{\otimes n}.
\]
The signs are drawn once for the entire sample, and each mixture consists of exactly \(n\) original observed records.

c41b911158936c70833f4af358257325952893db.title: Dyadic naming policies \(\mathsf N,\mathsf N_0\)
c41b911158936c70833f4af358257325952893db.body:
A dyadic name for a real number \(v\) is a sequence of nested closed intervals with dyadic rational endpoints that contain \(v\) and have width at most \(2^{-q}\) at each integer precision \(q\ge0\). The product coding of these sequences uses the discrete measurable structure on rational responses.

An admissible naming policy \(\mathsf N\) is a sequence of policies, one for each sample size \(n\), satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Public exponents.)} Valid names for \(\alpha,\beta\) are selected by Borel functions of the public pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) alone, before sampling.
\item \textbf{(Observed covariates.)} Valid names for the \(n\) observed covariates are selected by Borel functions of \((\alpha,\beta,\mathcal O)\), where \(\mathcal O\) is the tuple of original observed records.
\item \textbf{(Separate arithmetic input.)} The arithmetic engine is independently fixed, and name selection supplies the real-input representations used with that engine.
\end{itemize}
The interval procedure receives these selected names and the exact binary labels. Name selection is an input convention.

The dyadic-floor policy \(\mathsf N_0\) assigns every real input \(v\) the intervals
\[
\mathsf N_0(v)_q
=
\left[
2^{-q}\lfloor2^qv\rfloor,\;
2^{-q}\bigl(\lfloor2^qv\rfloor+1\bigr)
\right],
\qquad q\ge0.
\]
This is a valid name also at dyadic inputs and selects one concrete member of the policy-indexed interval family.

At the rank step, the queried exponent intervals are intersected with the known compact boxes
\[
\alpha\in[0,1],\qquad \beta\in[0,1/4].
\]
A syntactically malformed queried prefix or an empty intersection may yield the full effect interval. At the endpoint precision, the supplied exponent and observed-covariate intervals are passed raw to the endpoint expression tree, and the integer ranks selected at the rank step are retained. Outputs may vary across valid names.

9a9460bbe23a5de9edf4d0f659bccaee2a6beaaf.title: The logistic map
9a9460bbe23a5de9edf4d0f659bccaee2a6beaaf.body:
The logistic map \(\ell:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by
\[
\ell(t)=\frac{1}{1+\exp(-t)},\qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]

f0bc7f90f253aeb153634756e79d9f928d06259d.title: Log odds transformation
f0bc7f90f253aeb153634756e79d9f928d06259d.body:
The log-odds map \(\operatorname{logit}\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by
\[
\operatorname{logit}(t)=\log\!\left(\frac{t}{1-t}\right),
\qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
Here \(\log\) is Lean's totalized real logarithm and the quotient uses totalized real division. On \(0<t<1\), this is the usual log-odds transformation.

587186ead54933baafb1a1a37d91d0e837e3f598.title: Frontier pair \((\rho,I^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathsf E,\mathsf N})\)
587186ead54933baafb1a1a37d91d0e837e3f598.body:
The frontier pair consists of the expected-length profile \(\rho\) and the attaining procedure sequence \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\), defined by
\[
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r),
\qquad
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}
=
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N},
\]
for every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible naming policy \(\mathsf N\) of \(\cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine,obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}\). The diagnostic envelope and upper-construction output are those of \(\cref{obj:def:diagnostic-envelope,obj:def:upper-handle}\). The concrete sequence is
\[
I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0},
\]
where \(\mathsf E_0\) is the explicit rational arithmetic engine supplied by \(\cref{obj:lem:concrete-arithmetic-engine}\), and \(\mathsf N_0\) is the dyadic-floor naming policy.

The model and coverage conditions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design and logistic relation.)}
The uniform design and homogeneous logistic relation are specified in \(\cref{obj:ass:uniform-design,obj:ass:homogeneous-logit}\).
\item \textbf{(Envelopes and smoothness.)}
The effect, propensity, and prognosis envelopes and the native Hölder bounds are specified in \(\cref{obj:ass:effect-envelope,obj:ass:propensity-envelope,obj:ass:prognosis-envelope,obj:ass:propensity-holder,obj:ass:prognosis-holder}\).
\item \textbf{(Radius and honesty.)}
The evaluation radius and global coverage requirement are specified in \(\cref{obj:ass:evaluation-radius,obj:ass:global-coverage}\).
\end{itemize}
The logistic class, ambient model, radius slice, honest procedures, and minimax expected-length objective are those of \(\cref{obj:def:logistic-class,obj:def:model,obj:def:radius-model,obj:def:honest-procedures,obj:def:length-objective}\), with the causal extension of \(\cref{obj:def:causal-extension}\). Write \(c_\star\), \(C_\star\), and \(n_0\) for the lower comparison constant, upper comparison constant, and sample-size threshold selected in the sharp comparison of \(\cref{obj:thm:sharp-honest-frontier}\).

Each interval is the literal rational output of the same fixed-budget expression tree evaluated with the supplied fixed engine and valid dyadic interval representations, as in \(\cref{obj:lem:fixed-budget-realization}\). Different engines or representations may yield different rational intervals satisfying the endpoint enclosure bounds. Every member uses the observable numerator and denominator coordinates \((C,S)\) of \(\cref{obj:lem:observable-odds}\), the ordered-pair projection statistic of \(\cref{obj:def:projection-statistic}\), the separate projection resolutions of \(\cref{obj:def:resolutions}\), the coordinate estimates of \(\cref{obj:def:coordinate-estimates}\), and the joint inversion in the upper construction. Projection control and finite-sample honesty are given by \(\cref{obj:lem:projection-control,obj:thm:finite-honest-upper}\). The represented inputs are \((n,\alpha,\beta,\mathcal O)\), where \(\mathcal O\) is the tuple of original observed records, with representations selected by \(\mathsf N\) and independently fixed engine \(\mathsf E\); the radius \(r\) indexes the expected-length profile.

The converse uses the continuous calibrated priors of \(\cref{obj:def:calibration-maps,obj:def:continuous-calibrated-priors}\), with admissible native propensity and prognosis perturbations, one common scalar effect per draw, analytic singleton matching, and factorization across disjoint latent-sign components conditional on the original covariates, as established in \(\cref{obj:lem:scalar-implicit-function,obj:lem:exact-calibrations,obj:lem:calibrated-support,obj:lem:original-record-mixtures}\). Together with the parametric null floor of \(\cref{obj:lem:parametric-null-floor}\), this converse applies independently of the arithmetic engine and naming policy. The resulting frontier pair and concrete attaining sequence are those of \(\cref{obj:thm:full-honest-frontier-solution,obj:thm:full-honest-frontier-answer}\).

7c71915097231b69150e56919aee0695d9ad4913.title: Projection ranks $k_C$ and $k_S$
7c71915097231b69150e56919aee0695d9ad4913.body:
The inputs are \(n\ge2\), the public exponents \(\alpha,\beta\), a fixed admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\), and a policy \(\mathsf N\) supplying valid rational approximations to the public exponents.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the public precision budget and target resolutions by
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad
R_C=n^{2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)},\qquad
R_S=n^{2/(4\beta+1)}.
\]
For every positive integer \(b\), evaluate the logarithmic ceiling by integer comparisons:
\[
\lceil\log_2 b\rceil
=\min\{q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:2^q\ge b\}.
\]
Here \(b\) denotes an integer base.

\item At precision \(q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)\), obtain the exponent approximations supplied by \(\mathsf N\) and intersect their ranges with \([0,1]\) and \([0,1/4]\), respectively. Compute the ranges of \(2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)\) and \(2/(4\beta+1)\) by exact rational range operations, then apply the positive-integer-base power map of \(\mathsf E\) at that same precision. Denote the resulting rational enclosures by
\[
R_C\in[a_C,b_C],\qquad R_S\in[a_S,b_S].
\]
Here \(b_C,b_S\) are upper endpoints of resolution enclosures.

\item Output the integer ranks
\[
k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_C\rceil,\qquad
k_S(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_S\rceil.
\]
These ranks are fixed before sampling: \(\mathsf E\) is fixed, and the exponent approximations supplied by \(\mathsf N\) depend solely on the public exponents. Different admissible engines or valid approximations may produce different integers. Enclosure-width bounds, rank-factor bounds, and finite termination are properties of this construction.
\end{enumerate}

e8931fd643f3c84373b8115802e65b0900a92429.title: Coordinate estimates $\widehat C_n$ and $\widehat S_n$
e8931fd643f3c84373b8115802e65b0900a92429.body:
The exact real sample coordinates are
\[
\widehat C_n
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n A_iY_i-\mathbb U_{n,k_C}(A,Y),\qquad
\widehat S_n
=\mathbb U_{n,k_S}\bigl(A(1-Y),(1-A)Y\bigr),
\]
where, for \(n\ge2\), the retained ranks are
\[
k_C=k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N),\qquad
k_S=k_S(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N).
\]
Both ranks are selected by the fixed-budget resolution construction with the same admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and the public exponent approximations supplied by \(\mathsf N\). The upper construction uses this same engine and the supplied covariate approximations to enclose the finite sums at these retained ranks. The statistics \(\widehat C_n,\widehat S_n\) estimate the observable numerator and denominator coordinates \(C(P),S(P)\), respectively.

381a7bd748517853d0b422a341d00db5c7a4267f.title: Rational interval $I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)$
381a7bd748517853d0b422a341d00db5c7a4267f.body:
The inputs are the sample, \(n\ge1\), the public exponents \(\alpha,\beta\), a fixed admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\), a Borel policy \(\mathsf N\) supplying valid rational approximations to the exponents and observed covariates, and \(s_0\), the uniform positive lower bound for the denominator coordinate.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For \(n=1\), output
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{1,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=[-1/2,1/2].
\]
For \(n\ge2\), perform the remaining steps.

\item Select and retain the ranks
\[
k_C=k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N),\qquad
k_S=k_S(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)
\]
using the fixed rank budget and the exponent approximations supplied by \(\mathsf N\). Form the exact real coordinates at these ranks:
\[
\widehat C_n
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n A_iY_i-\mathbb U_{n,k_C}(A,Y),\qquad
\widehat S_n
=\mathbb U_{n,k_S}\bigl(A(1-Y),(1-A)Y\bigr).
\]

\item Define the smoothness sum, variance envelope, and coordinate error radii by
\[
s=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
V_n(k)=\frac{10}{n}+\frac{4k}{n(n-1)},
\]
\[
b_C=8k_C^{-s}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_C)},\qquad
b_S=25k_S^{-2\beta}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_S)}.
\]
Here \(b_C,b_S\) denote error radii.

\item Define truncation, the confidence-rectangle endpoints, and the inversion map by
\[
\operatorname{clip}_{[l,u]}(v)=\max\{l,\min\{u,v\}\},
\]
\[
c_\pm=\widehat C_n\pm b_C,\qquad
s_\pm=\operatorname{clip}_{[s_0,1]}(\widehat S_n\pm b_S),
\]
\[
F(c,d)=
\log\!\left(
\operatorname{clip}_{[\exp(-1/2),\exp(1/2)]}(1+c/d)
\right).
\]
The ideal exact real endpoints are
\[
L=\min\{F(c_-,s_-),F(c_-,s_+)\},\qquad
R=\max\{F(c_+,s_-),F(c_+,s_+)\}.
\]
Here \(R\) denotes the upper interval endpoint.

\item Define the retained maximum rank and endpoint precision budget by
\[
K=\max\{k_C,k_S\},\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)
=44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil
+4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil.
\]
At this one precision, obtain the supplied rational approximations to both exponents and all observed covariates. Evaluate the displayed finite expressions with the primitive maps of the same engine \(\mathsf E\) at precision \(q_{\mathrm{end}}\), together with exact rational range operations in the displayed expression tree, retaining \(k_C,k_S\). The resulting rational endpoint enclosures satisfy
\[
L_-\le L\le L_+,\qquad R_-\le R\le R_+.
\]
For valid inputs with
\[
0<\beta<1/4,\qquad \beta<\alpha\le1,\qquad n\ge2,
\]
they satisfy
\[
L_+-L_-\le\frac1n,\qquad R_+-R_-\le\frac1n.
\]

\item Output the closed rational interval
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
=
\left[
\max\{-1/2,L_-\},
\min\{1/2,R_+\}
\right].
\]
For the valid inputs specified above, this interval is nonempty and satisfies
\[
[L,R]\subseteq I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta),
\qquad
\left|I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\right|
\le R-L+\frac2n.
\]
The construction terminates after the two fixed precision budgets. Its sample map is Borel for an admissible \(\mathsf E\) and Borel \(\mathsf N\), and its inputs consist of the sample and public quantities displayed above. Different admissible engines or valid rational approximations may yield different rational endpoints.
\end{enumerate}

4a14bcb3f0fb90a5d265f068621ebecc26124e20.title: Calibration maps $\mathfrak c,\mathfrak B,\mathfrak q,\mathsf T,\mathfrak H,\mathfrak p$
4a14bcb3f0fb90a5d265f068621ebecc26124e20.body:
The covariance adjustment and its effect-normalized counterpart are
\[
\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2dv_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},\qquad
\mathfrak B(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2D(t)v_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},
\]
where \(\xi,\upsilon\) are scalar margins near \(1/2\), and
\[
d=\exp(t)-1,\qquad
v_*=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon),
\]
\[
L_*=1+d\{\xi(1-\upsilon)+(1-\xi)\upsilon\},\qquad
D(t)=\int_0^1\exp(st)\,ds.
\]
Here \(s\) is an integration variable. These formulas apply on the domain where the displayed square root and denominator are positive.

For two independent uniform signs \(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_1\), define
\[
Z_u=\epsilon_0\cos(\pi u/2)+\epsilon_1\sin(\pi u/2).
\]
Expectations below are over these signs. Let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}>0\) be the radius of the fixed signed open amplitude square on which the mixed calibration branch exists uniquely. On
\[
|\eta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad
|\zeta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad
u\in[0,1],
\]
define the mixed calibration root by
\[
\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)
=
\text{the unique }q\in(3/4,5/4)
\text{ satisfying }
16E\mathfrak B
\bigl(32\eta\zeta,1/2-\eta qZ_u,1/2+\zeta Z_u\bigr)-q=0.
\]
The smaller closed amplitude squares used for support and mixture bounds are contained in this domain.

For the separate fair-prior maps, define the baseline risk and local variance by
\[
p_*=2/5,\qquad v_*=p_*(1-p_*)=6/25.
\]
Here \(v_*\) denotes the fair-branch Bernoulli variance. Define
\[
\mathsf G(t,\xi)
=\frac{\exp(t)\xi}{1+\{\exp(t)-1\}\xi},\qquad
B_*=1+\{\exp(t)-1\}p_*,
\]
\[
\mathsf T(t,\delta)
=t+
\log\left(1-\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{p_*B_*}\right)
-\log\left(1+\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{(1-p_*)B_*}\right).
\]
On the fair core \(0\le t\le1/4\), for \(t\delta\ne0\), the normalized fair-matching residual is
\[
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)
=
\frac{
E\mathsf G(t,\xi+\delta Z_u)
-\mathsf G(\mathsf T(t,\delta),\xi)
}{t\delta^2}.
\]
The symbol \(\mathfrak H\) also denotes its removable smooth extension to the fixed open calibration neighborhood, including across \(t=0\), \(\delta=0\), and the spatial endpoints. The displayed quotient identity applies on the fair core.

Let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}}>0\) be the signed fair-amplitude radius, and let \(b\in(0,1/10)\) be the fixed sufficiently small bracket half-width about \(p_*\). Here \(b\) denotes a bracket half-width. The fair parameter domain contains
\[
0\le t\le1/4,\qquad
|\delta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}},\qquad
u\in[0,1],
\]
together with the fixed open neighborhood of these parameters, including signed parameters across \(t=0\) and the spatial endpoints. The denominators and logarithm arguments in the fair formulas are positive on this neighborhood. At \(t=0\) or \(\delta=0\), \(\mathfrak H\) is interpreted through its removable smooth extension.

On this neighborhood, define the fair calibration root by
\[
\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)
=
\text{the unique }\xi\in(p_*-b,p_*+b)
\text{ satisfying }\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)=0.
\]
Selection in the larger bracket \((3/10,1/2)\) gives this same root on the stated neighborhood. The smaller closed amplitude neighborhood used for support and mixture bounds is contained in this fair domain, uniformly over \(t\in[0,1/4]\) and \(u\in[0,1]\). The local branches are defined on the stated domains, where their existence, uniqueness, regularity, and matching properties hold.

fc43c9b441034daf35f0d984e4d3d352b77504fe.title: Uniform honesty and length bound
fc43c9b441034daf35f0d984e4d3d352b77504fe.body:
There exists an absolute constant \(K_0>0\) such that the following guarantees hold for every choice satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arithmetic engine.)} \(\mathsf E\) is an admissible, independently fixed deterministic rational interval-arithmetic engine satisfying the quantitative contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine}.
\item \textbf{(Naming policy.)} \(\mathsf N\) is an admissible Borel policy satisfying \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}, selecting valid names for the public exponents and observed covariates, with public exponent names fixed independently of the sample.
\item \textbf{(Public exponents.)} The real exponents \(\alpha,\beta\) satisfy
\[
0<\beta<\frac14,\qquad \beta<\alpha\le1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The integer sample size \(n\) satisfies \(n\ge1\).
\end{itemize}

Let \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\) denote the measurable interval procedure given by the literal rational output of the upper construction, whose inputs are the engine, naming policy, sample size, public exponents, and observed records. This procedure satisfies
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)
\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\) is the class of globally honest procedures in \cref{obj:def:honest-procedures}.

For every \(r\in[0,1/2]\) and every observed law \(P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)\), the effect-radius model of \cref{obj:def:radius-model},
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda}
\left[
\left|I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)(\mathcal O,U)\right|
\right]
\le K_0\,d_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]
Here \(\mathcal O\) is the sample of original observed records, \(U\) is the independent randomization seed with uniform law \(\lambda\) on the unit interval, and \(d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\) is the diagnostic envelope of \cref{obj:def:diagnostic-envelope}. The same constant \(K_0\) applies to all the engines, naming policies, exponents, sample sizes, radii, and laws quantified above.

For every sample and seed, there exist rational endpoints \(l,u\) such that the output is the closed interval \([l,u]\) and
\[
-\frac12\le l\le u\le\frac12.
\]
When \(n=1\), every sample and seed yields the full interval \([-1/2,1/2]\).

3bba2bd24d9b51210d7feaf2bbcff07c2429b328.title: Fixed-budget realization and measurability
3bba2bd24d9b51210d7feaf2bbcff07c2429b328.body:
The dyadic-floor naming policy \(\mathsf N_0\) is admissible in the sense of \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}. Moreover, suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Engine and names.)} \(\mathsf E\) is an admissible rational interval-arithmetic engine in the sense of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine}, and \(\mathsf N\) is an admissible Borel naming policy in the sense of \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}.
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\) is an integer with \(n\ge2\).
\item \textbf{(Public exponents.)} The real smoothness exponents satisfy
\[
0<\beta<\frac14,\qquad \beta<\alpha\le1.
\]
\end{itemize}
For every record tuple \(\mathcal O\in([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})^n\), let \(k_C,k_S\) be the ranks selected according to \cref{obj:def:resolutions}, with target resolutions
\[
R_C=n^{2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)},\qquad
R_S=n^{2/(4\beta+1)}.
\]
The prescribed public budgets are
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)
=44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil
 +4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil,\qquad
K=\max\{k_C,k_S\}.
\]
At the rank budget, both rational target enclosures \([a_C,b_C]\) and \([a_S,b_S]\) are successfully returned and satisfy
\[
b_C-a_C\le1,\qquad b_S-a_S\le1,
\]
\[
R_C\le k_C<R_C+2\le3R_C,\qquad
R_S\le k_S<R_S+2\le3R_S.
\]
Here \(b_C,b_S\) denote the upper endpoints of the resolution enclosures.

For the endpoint construction, use \(b_C,b_S\) instead to denote the coordinate error radii
\[
b_C=8k_C^{-(\alpha+\beta)}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_C)},\qquad
b_S=25k_S^{-2\beta}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_S)},
\]
where \(V_n(k)\) is the public variance envelope at rank \(k\). Let \(\widehat C_n,\widehat S_n\) be the numerator and denominator coordinate estimates, and set
\[
c_\pm=\widehat C_n\pm b_C,\qquad
s_\pm=\operatorname{clip}_{[s_0,1]}(\widehat S_n\pm b_S),
\]
where \(s_0\) is the denominator floor. With \(F(c,d)\) denoting the clipped logarithmic inversion of the coordinate ratio, the ideal lower and upper endpoints are
\[
L=\min\{F(c_-,s_-),F(c_-,s_+)\},\qquad
R=\max\{F(c_+,s_-),F(c_+,s_+)\}.
\]
At the endpoint budget, rational enclosures \([L_-,L_+]\) and \([R_-,R_+]\) are successfully returned with
\[
L\in[L_-,L_+],\qquad R\in[R_-,R_+],\qquad
